sections.title: Official Curated Lists (English)
sections.body:
The following word lists are based on academic vocabulary lists by Browne, Culligan, and Phillips. All licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

• Essential English 1000 — NGSL (New General Service List)
• Business English 1000 — BSL (Business Service List)
• Academic Vocabulary (TOEFL/IELTS) — NAWL (New Academic Word List)
• TOEIC Core 600 — TSL (TOEIC Service List)

Source: www.newgeneralservicelist.com
License text: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

Changes made: Korean translations and bilingual example sentences (auto-generated by Google Gemini) were added on top of the original word lists for study purposes.

ShareAlike: If you redistribute these lists or create derivatives, you must license them under the same CC BY-SA 4.0 terms.

sections.title: Official Curated Lists (Korean — for native speakers)
sections.body:
The following list collects common Korean spelling confusions for Korean native speakers.

• Frequently Misspelled Korean 100 — 100 pairs across 5 categories: verb/adjective endings & conjugations, verbs & adjectives, loanword spelling, sai-siot, and idiomatic / affix patterns

Sources:
• Korean language norms by the National Institute of Korean Language (Hangeul Spelling, Loanword Spelling, Standard Language Rules, etc.) — freely usable under Korea Open Government License Type 1 (attribution; commercial use & modification permitted)
• Wiktionary entries on Korean orthography (en.wiktionary.org) — CC BY-SA 4.0

Note: The headwords (pairs of correct vs. commonly-misspelled forms) are factual information defined by Hangeul Spelling rules and are not subject to copyright.

Changes made: 100 pairs were selected against the official norms and dictionaries, with definitions, distinguishing guides, and example sentences added (auto-generated by Google Gemini) for study purposes.

KOGL info: https://www.kogl.or.kr/info/license.do

sections.title: Use of Service
sections.body: Avocado (the 'App') is a personal vocabulary learning tool. By using the App, you agree to these terms.

sections.title: User Content & Copyright
sections.body:
You are solely responsible for the copyright of any content (words, meanings, example sentences, etc.) that you create or share in the App.

Do not share content that infringes on others' copyrights. Sharing content from copyrighted sources (dictionaries, textbooks, etc.) without permission is prohibited.

Prohibited content: adult/violent/hateful material, harassment of others, advertising/spam, clearly false information, personal data.

sections.title: Community Reporting & Moderation
sections.body:
If you find objectionable content in a shared word list, you can report it using the flag button at the top of the list detail screen. Choose a reason: inappropriate content, copyright infringement, spam, misinformation, or other.

Reports are reviewed by the operator. Confirmed violations result in the offending list being unpublished or deleted, and repeat-violator accounts may have their sharing privileges restricted. We may not respond to individual reports.

Repeated false reports may lead to reporting privileges being limited.

sections.title: Official Curated Lists
sections.body: Official word lists provided in the App (TOEIC, academic, etc.) are based on open-licensed data (CC BY-SA 4.0) and AI-generated content. Sources are noted in each list's description.

sections.title: AI Features & Daily Quota
sections.body:
AI autocomplete, word generation, and photo scan are offered through two paths:

1) Operator key (default): Signed-in users receive a daily quota — Free 100 words/day, Pro 1,000 words/day, resetting at midnight KST. Free users may watch optional rewarded ads to add +50 words each (up to +200/day).

2) Bring-your-own-key (BYOK): Register your own Gemini API key under Settings → Advanced Settings. No quota applies, but you cover the API costs. The key is stored only in this device's SecureStore and never touches our servers.

The developer does not guarantee the accuracy of AI-generated content.

sections.title: Pro Subscription & Billing
sections.body:
Pro subscription is provided through {{store}} in-app billing. Annual billing saves ~23% vs. monthly; the exact localized price is shown on the app's Plans screen.

Free trial: Any free trial is an offer from {{store}}, applied when you start a Pro subscription from the Plans screen. Whether it is offered, and for how long, is shown at store checkout. Cancel during the trial and you won't be charged; if you don't cancel, the first payment is taken when the trial ends.

Pro benefits: no ads, 1,000-word/day AI quota, uninterrupted experience.

Renewal & cancellation: Recurring billing follows {{store}} policy. Cancel anytime via {{manageSubscription}}. Pro benefits remain active until the end of the prepaid period.

Refunds follow {{store}}'s refund policy and must be requested through {{store}}.

sections.title: Advertising
sections.body:
Free users see Google AdMob banner ads, and may optionally watch rewarded ads to extend the daily AI quota. Pro subscribers see no ads.

The App uses the Android Advertising ID for ad serving only and does not combine it with other identifiers. To revoke consent or reset the Advertising ID, use System Settings → Google → Ads.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.body:
If you use Google Sign-In, your email and display name are used to operate the service. Vocabulary data is stored securely on Supabase and is never sold or shared with third parties.

When you subscribe to Pro, the {{store}} purchase token and product ID are stored to verify subscription status. Payment instrument details (card number, etc.) are handled exclusively by {{store}} and are never stored by us. See the Privacy Policy for full details.

sections.body: The App is provided as-is. The developer is not liable for damages resulting from service interruptions, data loss, or AI translation errors.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.noAnswerDesc: Ask directly and we'll look into it and reply.

items.q: What's the difference between Guest mode and signing in?
items.a:
Guest mode stores your lists only on this device — they'll be lost if you uninstall or switch devices.
Signing in with Google or Apple stores your data in the cloud, keeping it safe across devices and syncing automatically.

items.q: Can I sign in with Apple instead of Google?
items.a:
Yes — on iPhone and iPad you can sign in with Apple too. Cloud backup and multi-device sync work the same either way.

If the email matches, your Google and Apple sign-ins link to a single account automatically. Note: Apple's "Hide My Email" may create a separate account.

items.q: Where should I begin?
items.a:
1. Import a list from the Curation tab, or create your own from the Lists tab.
2. Add words (manual, AI auto-complete, photo scan, and more — 6 methods in total).
3. Start studying with Flashcards or Quiz.

items.q: Can I change which tab opens when I launch the app?
items.a: Yes — go to Settings → Display → Startup screen and choose Home, Lists, or Curation.

items.q: How many ways are there to add words?
items.a:
Six ways:
• Manual entry
• AI auto-complete (enter the word, AI fills meaning/example)
• AI generate (give a topic, AI builds a list)
• Photo scan (capture textbooks/notes)
• Spreadsheet paste (copy from Excel/Google Sheets)
• Voice input

You can also import other users' lists from the Curation tab.

items.q: Which method should I use?
items.a:
Manual for one or two words, AI auto-complete when you only know the word, AI generate when you have a topic, photo scan for textbooks/notes, spreadsheet paste for organized lists.

Auto-complete, generate, and photo scan all work out of the box. A daily quota is included even on the free tier.

items.q: Can I build vocab lists in languages other than Korean?
items.a:
Yes. On the Add Word screen, you can pick an input language and a meaning language independently from English, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Spanish (e.g., English → Korean, Japanese → Korean, Korean → Vietnamese).

AI auto-complete and photo scan work in all six languages, and the Curation tab has lists for each language too.

items.q: How does AI auto-complete work?
items.a:
Type just the word and tap auto-complete — AI fills in the meaning, example, pronunciation, and part of speech. Edit or regenerate if you don't like the result.

Each auto-complete call counts as 1 word against your daily quota.

items.q: What about AI generate?
items.a:
Enter a topic like "TOEIC business" or "100 travel English" and AI creates a word list. Pick the words you like and import only those.

One AI-generate set (~20 words) counts as 20 words against your daily quota.

items.q: What kinds of photos can be scanned?
items.a:
Both printed lists/textbooks and handwritten notes work. English, Korean, Japanese, and Chinese pages are all supported, and AI fills in the word, meaning, example, and pronunciation together.

Blurry photos or pages packed with too many words reduce accuracy. A photo scan costs 5 words for extraction plus 1 word per recognized word against your daily quota (common words you already have are free).

items.q: How does spreadsheet paste work?
items.a:
Copy a single column of words from Excel or Google Sheets and paste it in.

Meanings and examples are filled in by AI auto-complete, so you only need the word itself. Any language works — English, Korean, Japanese, and more.

If tabs or commas are present, only the first column is used as the word. Header rows are auto-detected and skipped.

items.q: Can I add words by voice?
items.a: Yes — tap the mic icon and say the word. You'll need to grant microphone permission the first time.

items.q: What happens if I edit the word while auto-complete is running?
items.a:
The search in progress is cancelled right away and restarts for the word you just typed. While it runs, the word being looked up is shown under the input field.

Saving is blocked until the result arrives — otherwise you'd save a half-filled word with no meaning or example.

Note that cancelling doesn't refund quota already spent: the server may have started working on it already.

items.q: What study modes are available?
items.a:
• Flashcards — flip cards to memorize
• Quiz — multiple choice to check yourself
• Examples — learn through context
• Autoplay — listen and shadow

items.q: What's the minimum to start studying?
items.a: You need at least 2 words to start a session.

items.q: Can I study a subset of words?
items.a:
Yes. Open a list and use the top filter to narrow to "Starred" or "Unmemorized", then study only those.

For multi-list combinations or finer control, use Pick & Study on the Home tab.

items.q: What is Pick & Study?
items.a:
It's a screen for gathering exactly the words you want across several lists. Open it from the Pick & Study card on Home.

Narrow things down with chips — status (unmemorized, memorized, missed, starred), part of speech, scope (lists and Days), and tags. There are ready-made presets too, like Most missed and Recently added. As soon as one condition is set, the matching words and their count appear, and you start from the study bar below by choosing Flashcards or Quiz.

Whatever you started with is kept as "Last used", so you can re-apply it with one tap next time. The conditions themselves reset when you restart the app.

One more thing: the one-tap buttons on Home (review, most missed, starred) always open as Flashcards. To use Quiz, choose it in Pick & Study or in a list's detail screen.

items.q: Is my progress saved if I stop mid-session?
items.a: Yes. Next time you open the same list, tap "Continue" to resume from where you left off.

items.q: I want to review only the words I missed.
items.a: On the results screen, tap "Restudy wrong words".

items.q: What is "Today's Review" on the Home screen?
items.a:
It automatically gathers words you learned earlier that are now due for a refresh. Tap the banner near the top of Home to start reviewing right away.

Words you get right come back at longer and longer intervals; words you miss return sooner. There's nothing to switch on — it builds up naturally as you study.

items.q: How are review words chosen?
items.a:
A word becomes a review candidate once enough time has passed that you're about to forget it. Well-known words stretch to longer intervals and appear rarely; frequently-missed words show up more often.

Each day's review is capped at 20 words so it never piles up too much.

items.q: How do I turn review reminders on or off?
items.a:
Go to Settings → Review reminders to toggle them and change the reminder time (once a day).

Reminders only arrive on days you have words to review — none are sent on empty days. The first time words are due, we'll ask once whether you'd like reminders.

items.q: I'm not getting review reminders.
items.a:
1. Check that Settings → Review reminders is on.
2. No reminder is sent on days with nothing to review — that's normal.
3. Notifications for Avocado may be off in your device settings, or Focus / Do Not Disturb may be on.

items.q: Do I have to set up a study plan?
items.a: No. Plans are useful when you want daily portions managed automatically. Resetting a plan keeps your memorization records intact.

items.q: How do I start a study plan?
items.a: Open a list, go to Study Plan, and set the duration (days) and daily portion. Each day's portion can be completed with Flashcards or Quiz.

items.q: What if I miss a few days?
items.a: After 7 days of inactivity, you'll see a reset prompt. Once the period ends, the plan expires and you can do a focused session on the remaining words.

items.q: What is Free Study mode?
items.a: It runs through the whole list without a daily portion limit. Use it when you want to study freely without a plan.

items.q: How is the "study streak" counted?
items.a:
Study at least one word in a day and your streak goes up by 1. Skip a whole day and it resets to 0.

You can see your current and longest streak near the top of Home and on the "My Learning" screen.

items.q: Where can I see my study history?
items.a:
The stats area near the top of Home and the "My Learning" screen show your streak, total memorized words, and a calendar. Tap a studied day on the calendar to see the words you memorized that day.

Tap "Share" to save your record as an image and share it.

items.q: What's the difference between "reviewed" and "memorized"?
items.a: Reviewed is how many words you studied that day; memorized is how many you newly marked as memorized. Seeing the same word many times still counts as memorized only once.

items.q: Will my words disappear if I switch from Guest to Google?
items.a:
If this is your first sign-in on this device, your guest words upload to the cloud automatically.

If the same account is already in use on another device, you'll see a "Merge / Keep Cloud" dialog. Choose "Merge" to preserve your guest data.

items.q: Will my lists follow me to a new device?
items.a: Signed-in users: yes — sign in on the new device and they download automatically. Guest users: no.

items.q: When does sync happen?
items.a: About 30 seconds after a change, and immediately when you send the app to the background.

items.q: Can I use the app offline?
items.a: Studying, adding, and editing all work offline. Only AI features (auto-complete, generate, photo scan) need internet. Offline changes sync the next time you connect.

items.q: What if I edit the same word on two devices at once?
items.a: The most recent save wins. Avoid editing the same word simultaneously on multiple devices.

items.q: Can I back up a list to a file or move it elsewhere?
items.a:
Yes. On the Lists tab, tap the ⋯ button on a list card (or long-press it) and choose "Export CSV" — the word, meaning, pronunciation, part of speech, definition, example, and tags all go into one file you can open in Excel or another app.

"Import CSV" does the reverse, adding exactly what the file says. No AI is called, so it doesn't touch your daily quota.

If instead you have a bare list of words and want AI to fill in the meanings and examples, use Excel Upload.

items.q: What do I need to use AI features?
items.a:
Nothing extra — AI auto-complete, generate, and photo scan work out of the box. The free tier includes a daily quota.

If you want more, you can upgrade to Pro, watch a rewarded ad to extend your daily quota, or register your own Gemini API key under Advanced Settings. See the "Plans & Ads" section for details.

items.q: How accurate are the AI results?
items.a: AI uses Google Gemini, which handles common vocabulary very accurately. Specialized jargon or rare expressions may occasionally be off — you can always edit or regenerate.

items.q: Can I trust AI-generated words for serious study?
items.a: Yes for general use. For exams or certifications, double-check against official sources. Any incorrect meaning or example can be edited directly on the word.

items.q: Is my input used to train AI?
items.a: This app does not use your vocabulary data for any external model training. AI calls are routed to the Google Gemini API and are subject to Google's processing policy — see Google's terms for details.

items.q: AI isn't returning results.
items.a:
1. Check your internet connection.
2. You may have hit your daily quota — wait for the next reset, or watch a rewarded ad to extend it immediately.
3. If you're using your own key (Advanced Settings), the key may be expired or rate-limited.

items.q: What plans are there?
items.a:
• Free — all study and management features. AI daily quota: 100 words (300 for your first 24 hours after signing up). A small banner ad is shown at the bottom of the screen.
• Pro — annual billing saves ~23%. All ads removed + AI daily quota of 1,000 words. See the Plans screen for the exact localized price.

A free trial may be offered when you start Pro. Whether it applies, and for how long, is shown on the Plans screen and at store checkout.

items.q: How is the "word count" measured?
items.a:
AI calls are weighted by how heavy they are:
• AI auto-complete: 1 word per call
• AI generate (1 set, ~20 words): 20 words
• Photo scan (1 image): 5 words extraction + 1 word per recognized word

The unit reflects Gemini API consumption, so one photo costs more than several auto-completes.

items.q: What happens when I hit the daily quota?
items.a:
AI calls pause for the rest of the day. Two options:

1. Watch a rewarded ad to instantly add 50 words (up to 300 words per day).
2. Upgrade to Pro for a 1,000-word daily quota plus no ads.

Non-AI features (studying, editing) keep working regardless of quota.

items.q: How does the Pro free trial work?
items.a:
The store applies the free trial when you start a Pro subscription from the Plans screen. Whether it's offered, and for how long, is shown at checkout. During the trial there are no ads and your daily quota is the Pro one.

Cancel during the trial and you won't be charged. If you don't cancel, the first payment is taken when the trial ends.

Separately from any trial, your first 24 hours after signing up come with a larger 300-word AI quota.

items.q: How do I subscribe to or cancel Pro?
items.a:
Start a Pro subscription from Settings → Plans. Billing runs through the store you installed the app from.

Where you cancel depends on the store:
• Android — Google Play app → Menu → Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions
• iPhone/iPad — Settings app → Apple Account → Subscriptions

Pro features stay active until the period you already paid for ends. Refunds follow each store's policy and are requested through that store.

items.q: How are ads shown?
items.a:
On the Free tier, a small banner sits at the bottom of the screen, spaced well away from study answer buttons to avoid mis-taps.

If you want to extend your daily quota, you can opt in to watch a rewarded video ad on demand.

items.q: Are there ads during the trial?
items.a: No — a free trial is ad-free, exactly like Pro. Once the trial ends and you're back on Free, the banner ad returns. Staying on Pro removes ads entirely.

items.q: What is the Curation tab for?
items.a: It's a shared library where you can browse word lists shared by other users and import them into your own. Search and popularity sort are supported.

items.q: Can I share my list to Curation?
items.a: Only signed-in users (Google or Apple) can share. Guests can import only.

items.q: Does editing an imported list affect the original?
items.a: No. You receive a copy at the moment of import — add, delete, edit freely. You can also import only selected words.

items.q: Can I remove a list I shared?
items.a: You can remove your own shares. Copies others have already imported are unaffected.

items.q: How do I report an objectionable shared list?
items.a:
Open a list shared by another user in the Curation tab and tap the report (flag) icon at the top. Pick a reason — inappropriate content, copyright infringement, spam, misinformation, or other — and optionally add up to 500 characters of detail.

Reporting requires signing in, and you can report the same list only once. Submitted reports are reviewed and acted on. (The report button doesn't appear on lists you shared yourself.)

items.q: Where do the built-in word lists come from?
items.a: The built-in official lists (TOEIC, Korean SAT, etc.) are based on CC BY-SA 4.0 open data and AI-generated content. Each list's source is noted in its description, and the full list of open-source libraries and data sources is available under Settings → Open Source & Data Sources.

items.q: How do I change the app theme (skin)?
items.a: Settings → Display → Skin lets you pick from various character and color themes.

items.q: How do I change the app language?
items.a: Settings → Language → App language. Pick Korean or English, independent of your device's system language.

items.q: How do I change my nickname?
items.a: Settings → Account → Nickname. Up to 10 characters. If your account has a name attached, signed-in users get it as the initial default.

items.q: How can I quickly find a word?
items.a:
Tap "Search my words" at the top of the Lists tab to search everything you've saved by term, meaning, definition, or tag.

You can also start studying straight from the results — pick Flashcards or Quiz in the study bar below and the session opens with exactly the words on screen. Chips let you narrow further; it's the same screen as Pick & Study.

Words in hidden lists aren't searched.

items.q: Can I use my own Gemini API key? (Advanced)
items.a:
Yes — if you have a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio, register it under Settings → Advanced Settings. While your own key is in use, your daily quota is replaced by your key's own rate limits (as defined by Google).

The key is stored only in this device's secure storage. AI calls go directly from your device to Google — never through our servers. Most users don't need to set this up; the default quotas are plenty for typical study.

items.q: What happens to my lists if I sign out?
items.a: Signing out hides this device's lists. They'll all return when you sign back in with the same account.

items.q: How do I delete my account permanently?
items.a: Tap "Delete Account" at the bottom of Settings. This permanently erases your cloud data, local lists, and any lists you shared to Curation. It cannot be undone.

items.q: Can other people see my lists?
items.a: No. Only lists you explicitly share to Curation are visible to others.

items.q: If I send a message, where does the reply show up?
items.a:
Settings → Contact us lets you send bug reports, feature ideas, billing questions, and anything else. Guests can send too.

Replies arrive in the app: when one is waiting, the "Contact us" row in Settings is marked, and opening it shows the reply below the message you sent. Add your email and you'll get a copy by mail as well — leave it blank and the in-app reply still works.

Your app version, device, language, and list counts are sent along to help track the problem down; you can switch that off before sending. Up to 5 messages a day, and a reply may take a few days.

items.q: What is the "What's new in Avocado" sheet after an update?
items.a:
The first time you open the app after updating, it shows what changed — once only. Tap OK and it won't come back.

Past updates are always available under Settings → What's new.

items.q: Sync isn't working.
items.a:
1. Check your internet connection.
2. Send the app to the background and reopen it — sync triggers immediately on backgrounding.
3. If it still fails, sign out and sign back in.

items.q: My lists are missing.
items.a: If you were signed in: sign in with the same account to restore them. Guest users who reinstalled the app: data is unrecoverable.

items.q: AI calls keep failing.
items.a:
1. Check your internet connection.
2. You may have hit your daily quota — watch a rewarded ad to extend it, or wait until reset.
3. Very blurry photos or pages crammed with text can fail to scan.
4. If you're on your own key (Advanced Settings), the key may be expired or over its rate limit.

items.q: Ads feel too frequent.
items.a: Free-tier users see a banner ad at the bottom at all times. Upgrade to Pro to remove all ads. Rewarded ads (the ones that extend your quota) only play when you choose to watch them.
